name: Peter Paul Rubens
findings: Uses smoky black 1.6x more than the other paintings from the same museum(s), so camera and varnish are held equal (from 2218 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, ocher red turns up as a small accent in 75% of the paintings that hold it, 2.5x the archive's rate (from 2218 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, dark teal grey turns up as the lightest note in 50% of the paintings that hold it, 4.4x the archive's rate (from 2218 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, rust brown turns up as the shadow in 50% of the paintings that hold it, 2.1x the archive's rate (from 2218 paintings here).
Pairs leather with tawny orange more than chance would predict (3 of 2218 paintings here).
Pairs cinnamon with copper more than chance would predict (3 of 2218 paintings here).
His single largest palette family (smoky black, dark olive brown, dark walnut) covers 53% of his paintings here.
Keeps 4 distinct palette families here, from smoky black, dark olive brown to smoky black, dark chocolate brown.
